title: Determine Tipper/Station Status From Operator Station Stacklights
candidate_goal: Use the operator station stacklight color/flash/horn pattern to identify the current status of the corresponding tipper and station (including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and bagout/surepost indications).
summary: Operators can read the two stacklights at each operator station to determine the documented status of the corresponding tipper/station and related events (paused, tipping, disabled, starved, faulted, surepost/bagout, RMS error, and E-stop).
rough_steps: Go to the operator station for the affected tipper/station. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the two stacklights at the top of either side of the operator station frame.]
Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

If the source indicates a horn alarm pattern, also observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern. [Image support needed: HMI screen for manual control of the OptiSweep system, including tipper grippers, fault resets, and lamp test.]

Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings: Solid Blue (Tipper paused), Solid Green (Tipping in process), Solid Red (Estop activated), Solid White (AGV present post-tipping), Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error), Flashing Blue (Tipper disabled), Flashing Green (Tipper starved), Flashing Red (Tipper faulted), Flashing White (SurePost tote being sent), Flashing Yellow (AGV present pre-tipping), Flashing Green+Yellow+Green with long horn alarm (Sort starting), Flashing White with intermittent horn alarm (Bagout complete). [Image support needed: HMI screen for manual control of the OptiSweep system, including tipper grippers, fault resets, and lamp test.]

Stop and escalate if the observed stacklight pattern indicates Estop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green), since these indicate a critical system condition requiring support action. [Image support needed: HMI screen for manual control of the OptiSweep system, including tipper grippers, fault resets, and lamp test.]
expected_result: The operator can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color pattern (and horn alarm pattern when present) to one of the documented tipper/station statuses.
failure_or_escalation_notes: If the observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination, stop and escalate for assistance.
If Solid Red indicates Estop is activated, escalate immediately (do not attempt to clear remotely from this procedure).
If Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error, escalate for further diagnostics.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the operator station stacklights
Ability to observe stacklight color(s), solid vs flashing, and horn alarm pattern (long vs intermittent) when present
evidence_source_refs: manual_optisweep_om_v3: section_text lists stacklight meanings for Solid/Flashing colors and horn alarm patterns
extraction_notes: This is extracted as a procedural interpretation aid (reference-like) because the source provides explicit observable mappings from stacklight patterns to system states, without naming a separate live UI surface.

title: Initiate Left/Right Tipper Cycle Using Operator Station Push-Buttons (TIP vs SURE POST)
candidate_goal: Use the operator station push-buttons to start the correct left or right tipper tipping cycle based on whether the incoming tote is for Surepost packages, and verify the correct button flashing behavior before pressing.
summary: The operator station has four tipper-related push-buttons (TIP LEFT/RIGHT and SURE POST LEFT/RIGHT) plus an emergency stop. Yellow/green flashing indicates tote arrival and package type readiness; pressing the correct button initiates the tipping cycle only when a tote is gripped.
rough_steps: Stand at the operator station push-button panel and identify the five labeled controls: TIP LEFT, SURE POST LEFT, TIP RIGHT, SURE POST RIGHT, and the emergency stop push-button (Item 5). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the labeled push-buttons and their positions on the operator station panel.]

For the left tipper, observe whether the left-side button is flashing: yellow flashing indicates a tote with Surepost packages is being delivered; green flashing indicates other (non-Surepost) packages. [Image support needed: figure or source depiction of flashing yellow vs flashing green on the active tipper buttons.]

For the right tipper, observe whether the right-side button is flashing using the same rule: yellow flashing = Surepost tote delivery; green flashing = all other packages. [Image support needed: figure or source depiction of flashing yellow vs flashing green on the active tipper buttons.]

Press the corresponding button for the tipper you want to run: press the green button to initiate the tipping cycle for non-Surepost packages, or press the yellow button to initiate the tipping cycle for Surepost packages (after the appropriate bag is ready for the Surepost packages). [Image support needed: Photo of the OptiSweep operator station push-button panel, showing controls for left and right tipper cycles, Surepost tote modes, and the emergency stop.]

If a tipping cycle is already in process for one tipper, confirm that the other tipper’s button does not start flashing until the first cycle completes; if both sides have AGVs and are waiting, confirm both buttons can flash until you press one. [Image support needed: source depiction/figure or operator-station behavior description showing flashing suppression until the opposite cycle completes.]

If you press a tip button before a tote is in the gripper, confirm that the tipper ignores the command; only once a tote is gripped by the gripper should the corresponding tip button flash. [Image support needed: figure or source depiction of the 'button flashes only once tote is gripped' behavior.]
expected_result: The correct left or right tipper tipping cycle starts when you press the flashing button that matches the tote type (yellow for Surepost, green for other packages), and the button flashing behavior follows the documented rules (no flashing for the other tipper until the current cycle completes; command ignored if no tote is gripped).
failure_or_escalation_notes: If the pressed tip button does not start the tipping cycle and the corresponding button was not flashing (or you pressed before a tote was gripped), stop and wait until the correct button flashes.
If there is imminent danger to personnel or risk of equipment damage, use the emergency stop push-button only for that purpose.

title: Install and tension a replacement timing belt (counter-balance leg) to 471 N
candidate_goal: Replace the timing belt and set belt tension to the specified target so the belt is properly tensioned and secured before reassembly and operator-station restart.
summary: A hands-on installation procedure for OptiSweep timing belt replacement, including counter-balance positioning, equal tensioning of two screws, sonic tension meter settings, and final torque/fastener steps before restarting the operator station.
rough_steps: Place the new timing belt on the pulleys.
Slightly lift the counter-balance carriage, remove the M6 fastener supporting it, and lower the counter-balance carriage to rest on the lower hard stop.

Very lightly tighten the M8x25 screws holding the idler pulley assembly in place so the assembly is not loose, but it can slide under the fasteners. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the idler pulley assembly and the M8x25 screws location.]
Insert the two M6x35 tension screws until they make firm contact with the actuator base. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the two M6x35 tension screws and actuator base contact point.]
Equally tighten the tension screws to add tension to the belt, ensuring both screws are turned the exact same amount (same applied force).
Gradually increase tension until 471 N is reached (acceptable range 448 N to 494 N).
Check tension only on the counter-balance leg of the belt (counter-balance is not in the way and will not interfere with belt vibration).

If using a Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter, set: Mass = 4.86 g/m, Width = 20 mm, Span = 1200 mm. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the Gates 508c Sonic Tension Meter settings screen/controls.]
Adjust/check until three acceptable readings in a row are received. Note: excessive noise (e.g., forklifts beeping, conveyors running) can interfere with sonic meter readings.
Tighten the M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs) to lock the idler assembly in place.

Raise the counter-balance carriage back to mid-travel and insert the M6 socket-head screws for the carriage to rest against. [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the M6 socket-head screws and mid-travel rest position.]

Re-attach the A-axis belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring the belt clamp aligns with belt teeth and does not pinch the belt (belt may need slight movement to line up). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the A-axis belt clamp alignment with belt teeth.]

Re-attach the counter-balance belt clamp using the six M6x20 screws and Loctite®, ensuring alignment with belt teeth and no belt pinch (counter-balance may need to be lifted slightly for alignment). [Image support needed: photo/figure showing the counter-balance belt clamp alignment.]
Remove the M6 socket-head screws supporting the A-axis and counter-balance.
Reinstall the side panels.
Re-start the operator station (referenced as “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
expected_result: Belt tension is set to 471 N within the acceptable range (448–494 N), tension readings are acceptable for three consecutive checks (if using the sonic meter), idler assembly is locked by tightening M8x25 fasteners to 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs), and belt clamps are aligned with belt teeth without pinching before operator-station restart.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Stop and re-check if tension cannot be brought into the 448–494 N range or if three consecutive acceptable sonic meter readings cannot be obtained.
Stop and re-check clamp alignment if the belt appears pinched or the belt clamp does not align with belt teeth.
If excessive noise prevents stable sonic readings, reduce noise sources and re-check tension.

Torque tool capable of 21.2 Nm (188 in-lbs)
